What comes up in Campbelltown

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Re-clad house with original sheeting underneath

The commonest surprise in Campbelltown stock, and the reason the survey comes before the quote.

How it is handled
The survey opens up the covered areas, samples are taken, and removal and independent clearance happen before the structure is touched.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists working to the survey, then the machine once clearance is issued.

Knockdown on a sloping block

Where the demolition is the first half of a job that ends with a building platform.

How it is handled
Structure removed, then the cut taken in benches from the high side with each level stable before the next is opened.
What does it
Midi excavator able to work on a grade, tippers staged at the street.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Campbelltown

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Post-war and public housing era stock Consistent construction of a known era, which makes the survey predictable even though it still has to be confirmed by sampling.
  • Fibro behind later cladding Very common here, where a re-clad covered the original sheeting rather than removing it.
  • Sloping blocks Which bring a site cut, benching and sometimes retaining into scopes that would be flat work elsewhere.
  • Steady redevelopment Single dwellings going to duplex and multi dwelling, with the services and boundaries to sort first.

Campbelltown streets will generally take a tipper, and the fall across the block is the thing that shapes the job: it sets how much material is coming out and where a machine can safely stand while it does. On the steeper lots the cut is taken in benches from the high side.

Campbelltown questions

What people ask before we start

The house was re-clad in the 1990s. Is the fibro gone?
Often it is not. Re-cladding frequently covered the original sheeting instead of removing it, so it is still there behind the newer work. The survey opens up what a visual inspection cannot reach.
Does the slope change the price?
It changes the method, and the method sets the rate. A fall across the block means benching, a longer programme and more material out, and it decides where the machine can work from.
Why does the haul distance matter out here?
Because the destination is set by what the material is classified as rather than by what is closest, and from the south west the licensed facility for a given classification can be a long way off. It is a real line in the price rather than a rounding error.
Is the asbestos removal a separate engagement?
A separate licence, but not a separate engagement. Licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal and an independent licensed assessor issues the clearance, while Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and runs the programme across all of it.
